before: Enacted as 2026 Session Laws Chapter 140; section 31 effective 2026-07-01
after: Enacted as 2026 Session Laws Chapter 140, effective 2026-09-12; section 31 specifies an application and qualification prohibition from 2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30, with retroactive application

before: Section 31 imposes a three-year moratorium, 2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30, on new applications to the state data center tax relief program under A.R.S. 41-1519. It suspends eligibility for the incentive; it does not pause data center construction, siting, or local permitting.
after: Section 31 bars the Arizona Commerce Authority from accepting applications for new computer data centers and bars new centers from qualifying for tax relief under A.R.S. 41-1519 from 2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30; it does not pause construction, siting, or local permitting.
Section 31 is repealed from and after 2029-06-30.

before: Would require county comprehensive plans to designate enough land for data centers and small modular reactors so counties do not prevent effective siting.
after: Introduced bill would require qualifying county comprehensive plans to designate land for data centers and electric generating units, including small modular reactors, sufficient for their effective use; requirements apply to counties over 125,000 population and may be included by other counties.

before: Would create a colocation pathway for electric generating facilities serving data centers and other large loads, reducing certificate requirements for qualifying adjacent generation.
after: House-engrossed proposal would allow a utility to build a qualifying plant without a certificate of environmental compatibility after notice and public comment if colocated with an extra high load factor customer that has applicable zoning entitlements.
